'''Winslow Russell Briggs''' (April 29, 1928 – February 11, 2019) was an American plant biologist who introduced techniques from molecular biology to the field of plant biology.<ref name="Carnegie"/><ref name="MP2019"/> 
Briggs was an international leader in [[molecular biological]] research on plant sensing, in particular how plants respond to light for growth and development<ref name="Japan"/> and the understanding of both red and blue-light photoreceptor systems in plants.<ref name="MP2019"/><ref name="Huala">{{cite journal |last1=Briggs |first1=Winslow R. |last2=Huala |first2=Eva |title=Blue-Light Photoreceptors in Higher Plants |journal=Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology |date=November 1999 |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=33–62 |doi=10.1146/annurev.cellbio.15.1.33 |pmid=10611956 }}</ref>
His work has made substantial contributions to plant science, agriculture and ecology.<ref name="MP2019"/>

Briggs served as President of the [[American Institute of Biological Sciences]] in 1981.<ref name="MP2019"/> He was the [[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''Annual Review of Plant Physiology and Plant Molecular Biology'' (later the ''[[Annual Review of Plant Biology]]'') from 1973 to 1993.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1981 |first=Winslow R.|last=Briggs |title=Preface by Winslow R. Briggs| url=http://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.pp.32.101804.100001| journal=Annual Review of Plant Physiology| language=en|volume=32| issue=1| article-number=annurev.pp.32.101804.100001| doi=10.1146/annurev.pp.32.101804.100001|issn=0066-4294|url-access=subscription|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1972|first=Leonard |last=Machlis |title=Preface by Leonard Machlis|url=http://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.pp.23.100504.100001|journal=Annual Review of Plant Physiology|language=en|volume=23|issue=1|article-number=annurev.pp.23.100504.100001|doi=10.1146/annurev.pp.23.100504.100001|issn=0066-4294|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jones|first=Russell L.|date=1994|title=Preface by the Editor|url=http://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev.pp.45.101804.100001|journal=Annual Review of Plant Physiology and Plant Molecular Biology|language=en|volume=45|issue=1|article-number=annurev.pp.45.101804.100001|doi=10.1146/annurev.pp.45.101804.100001|issn=1040-2519|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Education==
Briggs graduated from [[Harvard University]] with a Bachelor of Arts in 1951, a Master of Arts in 1952, and a Doctor of Philosophy in 1956.<ref name="Marquis"/>

==Career==
Between 1955 and 1967, Briggs was an instructor in the Department of Biological Sciences at [[Stanford University]] and successively became an assistant professor in 1957. In 1962 he was promoted to associate professor and became a professor in 1966. In 1967 he moved to [[Harvard University]] as a professor in the Department of Biology.<ref name="Marquis"/>

In 1973 he returned to Department of Biological Sciences at Stanford University  as a professor and as a Director of the Department of Plant Biology, [[Carnegie Institution for Science]]. From 1993 until his death in 2019, he continued to do research as a director emeritus in the Department of Plant Biology at Carnegie Institution for Science.<ref name="memory"/>

In addition to memberships in the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS)<ref name="NAS"/> and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (AAAS),<ref name="Missouri"/> Briggs was a member of the [[American Institute of Biological Sciences]] (President in 1981),<ref name="MP2019">{{cite journal |title=In Memory of Winslow Briggs, a Luminary Who Shed Light on Plants and Enlightened People |journal=Molecular Plant |date=April 2019 |volume=12 |issue=April |pages=461–463 |doi=10.1016/j.molp.2019.02.007 |s2cid=243026180 |url=https://www.cell.com/molecular-plant/pdf/S1674-2052(19)30061-9.pdf |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref> 
the [[American Society of Plant Physiologists]] (chairman 1975-1976),<ref name="Carnegie"/> 
the [[Botanical Society of America]],<ref name="BSA"/>
the [[Nature Conservancy]],<ref name="Marquis"/>
and the [[American Society for Photobiology]].<ref name="McDowell"/>

==Research==
Briggs conducted research on the physiology and biochemistry in the development of plants in response to light. He made major contributions to understanding the biochemical and physical characteristics of photoreceptors of plants. He demonstrated through experiments that the phototropic bending of plant stems to follow a light source has its basis in the transport of [[auxin]]. 
He identified and studied both the red and far-red light
photoreceptors of plants and  the blue light receptor that
mediates [[phototropism]].  Using [[thale cress]] (''Arabidopsis thaliana'') Briggs was able to clone the gene for [[phototropin]].<ref name="MP2019"/><ref name="Wang">{{cite journal |last1=Kutschera |first1=Ulrich |last2=Wang |first2=Zhi-Yong |title=Light and plant development: the discovery of phototropins by Winslow R. Briggs (1928–2019) |journal=Plant Signaling & Behavior |date=3 October 2019 |volume=14 |issue=10 |article-number=e1652521 |doi=10.1080/15592324.2019.1652521 |pmid=31434535 |pmc=6768212 }}</ref><ref name="Kutschera">{{cite journal |last1=Kutschera |first1=Ulrich |last2=Briggs |first2=Winslow R. |title=Root phototropism: from dogma to the mechanism of blue light perception |journal=Planta |date=March 2012 |volume=235 |issue=3 |pages=443–452 |doi=10.1007/s00425-012-1597-y |pmid=22293854 |s2cid=9599754 }}</ref>

According to ISIHighlyCited, Briggs is one of the most cited scientists in the field of botany and zoology. Briggs was (co-) author of articles in journals such as ''American Journal of Botany, Nature, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, Science'' and ''Scientific American''.<ref name="Briggsprofile">{{Cite web|url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/winslow-briggs?tab=publications|title=Winslow Briggs' Profile &#124; Stanford Profiles|website=profiles.stanford.edu}}</ref> Along with John L. Spudich he was editor of the ''Handbook of Photosensory Receptors'' (2005).<ref name="Spudich">{{cite book |last1=Briggs |first1=Winslow R. |last2=Spudich |first2=John L. |title=Handbook of photosensory receptors |date=2005 |publisher=Wiley-VCH |location=Weinheim |isbn=978-3-527-60510-1 |url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Handbook+of+Photosensory+Receptors-p-9783527605101 |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>

He was an avid mountaineer and had scaled several prominent peaks.<ref name="Wandering">{{cite journal |last1=Briggs |first1=Winslow R. |title=A Wandering Pathway in Plant Biology: From Wildflowers to Phototropins to Bacterial Virulence |journal=Annual Review of Plant Biology |date=2 June 2010 |volume=61 |issue=1 |pages=1–20 |doi=10.1146/annurev-arplant-042809-112326 |pmid=20192732 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/full/10.1146/annurev-arplant-042809-112326 |access-date=11 October 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He was a volunteer at [[Henry W. Coe State Park]] for 40 years.<ref name="obit" /> He organized volunteers in 2007 to study the park's recovery from a wildfire, and discovered that the smoke contained chemicals that helped to stimulate the sprouting of seeds of rare plants that lie dormant and return after a fire.<ref name="Carnegie"/>

Briggs died on February 11, 2019, at Stanford Medical Center at the age of 90.<ref name="obit">{{cite web |author-first= Natasha |last= Metzler |title=Plant biologist Winslow Briggs dies at 90 |url=https://news.stanford.edu/2019/02/15/plant-biologist-winslow-briggs-dies-90/ |website=Stanford News |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=February 22, 2019 |language=en |date=February 15, 2019}}</ref><ref name="memory">{{cite web |title=In Memory of Winslow R. Briggs (1928-2019) |url=http://www.evolutionsbiologen.de/winslow-r-briggs.html |website=evolutionsbiologen.de |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Briggs received many honors during his career.  
* 1973, Guggenheim fellowship for natural sciences, US & Canada<ref name="Guggenheim">{{cite web |title=Winslow Briggs |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/winslow-briggs/ |website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>
* 1973, Certificate of Merit, [[Botanical Society of America]]
* 1974, Member, [[National Academy of Sciences|US National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS)<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=Winslow R. Briggs |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/winslow-r-briggs-vzhykx/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>
* 1975, Member, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (AAAS)<ref name="Missouri">{{cite web |title=Winslow Briggs Minding the gap—between guard cells December 3, 2012 |url=https://distinguishedvisitors.missouri.edu/2012/winslow-briggs/ |website=University of Missouri |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>
* 1983, Distinguished Fellow, [[Botanical Society of America]]<ref name="BSA">{{cite web |title=Distinguished Fellow of the Botanical Society of America |url=https://cms.botany.org/home/awards/awards-for-established-scientists/distinguishedfellow.html |website=Botanical Society of America |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>
* 1986, Member, [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Deutsche Akademie der Naturforscher Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/359/|title=List of Members|website=leopoldina.org|access-date=19 October 2017}}</ref> 
* 1995, Sterling Hendricks Medal, [[United States Department of Agriculture]] and the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Sterling B. Hendricks Memorial Lectureship |url=https://www.agrodiv.org/awards/sterling-b-hendricks-memorial-lectureship/ |website=AGRO Division |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>
* 2001, Bernard Axelrod Lecturer, [[Purdue University]]<ref>{{cite web |title=The Bernard Axelrod Lectures 2008 |url=https://ag.purdue.edu/biochem/Documents/Axelrod%20Lecturers/jasper_rine.pdf |website=Purdue University |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref>
* 2002, Honorary doctorate, [[Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg]]<ref name="Marquis"/>
* 2007, Adolph E. Gude, Jr. Award, [[American Society of Plant Biologists]]<ref name="Carnegie">{{cite web |title=Winslow Briggs, who discovered how plant seedlings grow toward light, dies at 90 |url=https://carnegiescience.edu/news/winslow-briggs-who-discovered-how-plant-seedlings-grow-toward-light-dies-90 |website=Carnegie Institution for Science |access-date=11 October 2021|date=February 12, 2019}}</ref>
* 2009, [[International Prize for Biology]], [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]]<ref name="Engen">{{cite journal |last1=Engen |first1=Katie |title=Japan Society for the Promotion of Science Awards International Prize for Biology to Winslow Briggs Emperor and Empress of Japan Preside at Prestigious Tokyo Ceremony |journal=ASPB News, THE NEWSLETTER OF THE AMERICAN SOCIETY OF PLANT BIOLOGISTS |date=2010 |volume=37 |issue=1 |pages=13–15 |url=https://aspb.org/newsletter/archive/2010/janfeb10.pdf |access-date=11 October 2021}}</ref><ref name="McDowell">{{cite news |last1=McDowell |first1=Tina |title=Award for Winslow Briggs |url=https://photobiology.org/pdf/newsletter/asp_nl210.pdf |access-date=11 October 2021 |work=ASP NEWS |publisher= American Society for Photobiology |issue=Autumn |date=2009}}</ref><ref name="Japan">{{cite news |title=Carnegie's Winslow Briggs Receives International Prize for Biology |url=https://carnegiescience.edu/news/carnegie%E2%80%99s-winslow-briggs-receives-international-prize-biology |access-date=11 October 2021 |work=Carnegie Institution for Science |date=September 16, 2009 |archive-date=October 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024172618/https://carnegiescience.edu/news/carnegie%25E2%2580%2599s-winslow-briggs-receives-international-prize-biology |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2010, Einstein Professor,  [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="EurekAlert">{{cite web |last1=Carnegie Institution for Science |title=Carnegie's Winslow Briggs elected Einstein Professor, Chinese Academy of Sciences Grant and Award Announcement |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/611856 |website=EurekAlert! |access-date=11 October 2021|date= 14 October 2010}}</ref>
* 2016, doctoral degree honoris causa, [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]<ref name="Marquis"/>
* 2018, Albert Nelson Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award, Marquis Who's Who<ref name="Marquis">{{cite web |title=Winslow Russell Briggs, Ph.D., Presented with the Albert Nelson Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award by Marquis Who's Who |url=https://www.24-7pressrelease.com/press-release/454680/winslow-russell-briggs-phd-presented-with-the-albert-nelson-marquis-lifetime-achievement-award-by-marquis-whos-who |access-date=11 October 2021 |website=Who's Who in America |date=July 10, 2018}}</ref>

Briggs has been recognized as a Pioneer Member of the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://aspb.org/membership/aspb-pioneer-members/ | title=ASPB Pioneer Members }}</ref>
